title: The Golf Ball That Got Dents
description: Golfers once thought smooth balls flew best, but dents create a thin turbulent layer that reduces drag and lets dimpled balls travel farther. #golf #physics #shorts
style: simple black stickman characters, round heads, dot eyes, thick outlines, flat bold backgrounds, 9:16

shots.narration: A golfer hammered 327 dents into his new ball before a village tournament.
shots.visual: Stickman golfer with yellow vest swings hammer at ball on tee; sign reads 327 DENTS

shots.narration: He faced the smooth-ball champion on the old hill course for a shiny silver cup.
shots.visual: Two stickmen face off across golf course; champion has striped cap and smooth ball; silver cup on pedestal

shots.narration: The champion laughed, "You wrecked your only ball, you clown."
shots.visual: Champion points and laughs; dented ball looks rough on ground

shots.narration: On the first drive, the smooth ball flew far, but the dented ball rolled past it.
shots.visual: Two balls in flight over hills; dented ball overtakes smooth ball

shots.narration: By hole 9, the champion stared as the weird ball kept sailing ahead.
shots.visual: Scoreboard shows hole 9; champion scratches head; golfer smiles

shots.narration: Then a hard wind blasted across the final hill toward the flag.
shots.visual: Wind lines sweep across hill; flag bends; both golfers brace

shots.narration: You see, tiny dents make air cling to the ball and cut drag through the wind.
shots.visual: Simple diagram: ball with dimples and airflow lines hugging surface, arrow shows less drag

shots.narration: The dented ball dropped beside the flag, and the champion demanded 327 dents.
shots.visual: Dented ball lands next to flag; champion holds hammer over smooth ball while golfer holds trophy
